name: area-scoring
title: area scoring
definition: Area scoring in weiqi computes each player's final score as the number of that player's own live stones remaining on the board plus the vacant points that count as that player's territory; captures made during play matter only insofar as they change which stones are on the board at the end, not as separately counted prisoner points. Chinese, New Zealand, and Ing rules all use area scoring. Because a stone on the board and an enclosed empty point are worth the same one point each, playing an extra move inside your own territory late in the game costs nothing under area scoring: it simply converts a territory point into a stone point.

name: atari
title: atari
definition: Atari in weiqi is the state in which a stone or connected group has only one liberty remaining and is therefore under immediate threat of capture.

name: capture
title: capture
definition: A capture in weiqi occurs when a move removes the last liberty from an opposing stone or connected group, after which those stones are removed from the board.

name: connection
title: connection
definition: A connection in weiqi is a relation between stones that makes them function as one group, sharing liberties and supporting each other's defense.

name: dame
title: dame
definition: Dame in weiqi are the neutral, empty points left on the board that border stones of both colors and belong to neither player's territory.

name: dead-stones
title: dead stones
definition: Dead stones in weiqi are stones left on the board after both players pass that cannot avoid eventual capture under correct play, and are therefore removed as though captured before the board is counted, without either player having to actually play out the capture. A stone or group is dead exactly when it fails the same test life-and-death reading always applies: it cannot make two secure eyes and cannot escape or be rescued. A group that shares unresolvable liberties with the opponent, by contrast, is in seki and is never marked dead.

name: eye
title: eye
definition: An eye in weiqi is an empty point or enclosed space inside a group's shape that functions as an internal liberty and helps determine whether the group can live.

name: false-eye
title: false eye
definition: A false eye in weiqi is an eye-shaped empty point that looks like a protected internal liberty but does not meet the diagonal-control and connection requirements of a real eye, so the opponent can eventually force the surrounding group to fill it.

name: handicap
title: handicap
definition: A handicap in weiqi is a rule adjustment, usually extra Black stones placed before play begins, that lets players of unequal strength compete in a meaningful game.

name: hoshi
title: hoshi
definition: Hoshi in weiqi are the nine marked star points on a 19x19 board, used as fixed handicap-stone locations and as visual landmarks for opening play, with the center star point known as tengen. The nine points sit at the 4-4 point in each corner, the 4-10 point on the midpoint of each edge, and the 10-10 point at the exact center of the board.

name: ko
title: ko
definition: Ko in weiqi is a repetition constraint that forbids a player from making the immediate recapture that would recreate the previous board position.

name: komi
title: komi
definition: Komi in weiqi is the point compensation added to White's final score to offset Black's first-move advantage.

name: liberty
title: liberty
definition: A liberty in weiqi is an empty intersection directly adjacent to a stone or connected group of stones. Liberties determine whether a group remains on the board. When the last liberty is removed, the group is subject to capture.

name: life-and-death
title: life and death
definition: Life and death in weiqi is the analysis of whether a group can secure enough stable shape, usually through eyes, to avoid capture, or whether the opponent can force it off the board.

name: pass
title: pass
definition: A pass in weiqi is a legal turn in which a player declines to place a stone, leaving the board unchanged and giving the move to the opponent. Passing is always available; it is never restricted by ko, suicide, or any other placement rule, since it places nothing. Two consecutive passes, one by each player in immediate succession, end the main phase of play and open dead-stones settlement and scoring; if the players cannot agree during that settlement, play conventionally resumes from the pass to resolve the disagreement by capture.

name: seki
title: seki
definition: Seki in weiqi is a standoff in which two or more groups of opposite color share their remaining liberties, and neither side can play into the shared liberties without reducing its own group to a liberty count the opponent can then capture on the next move. Neither group has two eyes, yet neither can be captured either, so both remain on the board unresolved for the rest of the game. Seki is a genuine third outcome for a local fight, distinct from either group living outright or dying.

name: suicide
title: suicide
definition: Suicide in weiqi is a move that would leave the moving player's own stone or group with zero liberties after any opposing stones it removes are taken off the board. Under most rulesets suicide is simply illegal: a player may not place a stone that reduces their own group to no liberties unless that same move first captures an opposing group and thereby restores at least one liberty. New Zealand rules are the well-known exception, permitting suicide of any size — a player may play a stone, or fill their own group's last liberties entirely, and the played stones are then immediately removed as self-captured.

name: superko
title: superko
definition: Superko in weiqi is a repetition rule that extends ko beyond the single immediately-preceding position: it forbids recreating any whole-board position that has already occurred in the game, not only the one position just before the opponent's last move. Two variants are in common use. Positional superko (PSK) forbids any recurrence of an identical arrangement of stones, regardless of whose turn it is. Situational superko (SSK) forbids a recurrence only when it is also the same player's turn to move as it was the earlier time that arrangement occurred — so the same stone arrangement may legally recur once with the other player to move, but not a second time with the original player to move.

name: territory
title: territory
definition: Territory in weiqi is the set of vacant points effectively enclosed by one player's stones and unavailable to the opponent except at unacceptable cost.

name: territory-scoring
title: territory scoring
definition: Territory scoring in weiqi computes each player's final score as the vacant points that count as that player's territory plus the prisoners that player captured from the opponent during the game; a live stone remaining on the board at the end contributes no direct point value of its own. Japanese and Korean rules use territory scoring. Because stones themselves are not counted, playing an extra move inside your own territory late in the game costs a full point under territory scoring: it removes one territory point and, since nothing was captured, adds nothing back.
